ImageDescription.value:
The Cathedral of Saint Mary of the See (Spanish: Catedral de Santa María de la Sede), better known as Seville Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Seville (Andalusia, Spain). It is the largest Gothic cathedral and the third-largest church in the world. After its completion in the early 16th century, Seville Cathedral supplanted Hagia Sophia as the largest cathedral in the world, a title the Byzantine church had held for nearly a thousand years. The cathedral also serves as the burial site of Christopher Columbus. The Archbishop's Palace is located on the northeastern side of the cathedral.

Categories.value: Cathedral of Seville|Almohad architecture|Cultural heritage|Self-published work

ImageDescription.value: Seville Cathedral, also known as the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the See, is one of the largest Gothic cathedrals in the world. It was built on the site of the former Almohad mosque, preserving the famous minaret, the Giralda, which now serves as its bell tower. It is notable for its enormous nave, its side chapels, and its impressive high altar. It houses works of art, royal tombs, and the tomb of Christopher Columbus. Its architecture combines Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque elements, reflecting centuries of history.
